analyses.failure: test_chk_028_reset_during_traffic [slv_slow.s1]: AssertionError 'CHK-031: transfer 1 has no completion edge C' raised from score(e, partial=True) at test_async_apb_bridge.py:967 -> :560. The same test passes in the other 13 run configurations (results.json:398-411). Only slv_slow.s1 fails.
analyses.spec_says: Reset: spec/AsyncAPBBridge_Design_Specification.md:149 (REQ-RESET-002, also rules.json:1425 AB2-3-39): "The two resets shall be asserted together ... A transfer in flight when a reset is asserted is lost." Spec line 533 (ERR-003, rules.json:5101 AB2-12-05): "The transfer is lost; the requester model repeats it after the release." contract.json:862 (CHK-028 behavior): "The transfer in flight never completes, and there is no spurious transfer after release". contract.json:864 (CHK-028 expected): "The interrupted transfer never produces o_apb_pready. Each repeated transfer and all later traffic pass the CHK-029 scoreboard." Definition of C at contract.json:947 (CHK-031): "Name C the i_clk_slv edge where o_apb_psel=1, o_apb_penable=1 and i_apb_pready=1 are sampled." contract.json:948: requester PREADY comes "at the j-th rising edge of i_clk_mst after C, with j in [N+1, N+3]". So a transfer whose PREADY has already reached the requester had a completion edge C before PREADY. It is a completed transfer, not one that was 'in flight' and lost.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_apbcdc_slv.sv:139 `w_done = (state==ACCESS) & i_apb_pready` at rising edge C. :179/:204 toggles reg_ack and :227-228 loads reg_resp_hold at that same edge, and :164-165/:205-206 drop psel/penable at C+1. The ack crosses through u_sync_ack (rtl/m_vlsit_apbcdc_mst.sv:276), then w_ack_event (:137) -> w_load_resp (:184) -> reg_pready (:215) -> o_apb_pready (:242). PREADY therefore needs the slv-side w_done, which needs a real C. The RTL cannot produce requester PREADY without C. In this run every SVA protocol check reports 0 fails (slv_slow.s1.log:525-542: CHK-003/004/006/015 etc. fails=0). Nothing shows that the DUT raised PREADY for transfer 1 incorrectly. The test recorded tP for it at test:270, so the DUT completed it before the reset.
analyses.test_does: Completer model (test:318-409) runs only on FALLING edges of i_clk_slv. At falling edge F_k it drives i_apb_pready=1 and stores c['resp'] (test:395-398). It records c['tC'] only at the NEXT falling edge F_k+1, about C+Ts/2, when it sees prev=(psel=1,penable=1) with drv_rdy=1 (test:370-372). The requester records tP at the i_clk_mst falling edge where it samples o_apb_pready=1 (test:263-270), that is (N+1..N+3)+MSYNC-extra mst cycles after C. The run uses CELL_TYPE=2 (N=2) and +APBCDC_MSYNC_EN=1 (slv_slow.s1.log:6,302). In the 'slv_slow' run T_slv is much longer than T_mst (inferred from the run name; the periods are not logged), so Ts/2 can be longer than j*T_mst. In that case tP is recorded BEFORE the completer has recorded tC. test_chk_028 then polls `e.ndone() >= base and e.match(ph)` (test:957-958; ndone counts reqs with 'tP', test:155-156). That condition can be true in this window. It calls assert_resets (test:959; it waits only Timer(100ps), test:516-526) and right away calls score(e, partial=True) (test:967). score keeps every req that has 'tP' (test:546) and requires 'resp' and 'tC' in the matching cpl (test:560). 'resp' is present (set at F_k) but 'tC' is not yet written. The 'NNC hand fix' that back-fills tC when the reset comes after C (test:335-339, condition e.t_rst > t) runs inside the completer coroutine at the next slv falling edge. That is AFTER score() has already raised, so it cannot help here. The expectation 'every transfer with tP has tC' is right under the spec. What is wrong is when the test samples it: the model's record of C lags the real edge C by half a slv period.

candidates.evidence_for: 1) The completer model writes tC only at the slv falling edge after C (test:370-372), which is Ts/2 after the real C. The requester records tP as soon as PREADY is sampled (test:270), and score() runs 100 ps after the reset (test:516-522, 959, 967) without waiting for a slv falling edge. When Ts/2 is longer than the PREADY crossing time (j in [N+1,N+3] mst edges plus MSYNC extra), tP exists without tC. This happens only when the slave clock is slow, which matches the failure in slv_slow.s1 alone (results.json:398-411) and the pass of the same test in slv_fast.s1 and the default runs (sim.log:421-424). 2) The existing hand fix (test:335-339) shows the authors already saw this race in a different ordering (reset seen by the completer before it records C). It is applied in the completer coroutine, so it cannot run before score() at test:967. 3) The spec ties PREADY to an earlier C (contract.json:948), and the RTL can only produce PREADY after a slv-side w_done (slv.sv:139, mst.sv:137/184/215). So C did happen, and only the model's record of it is missing. 4) 'resp' is set at F_k (test:397), so the missing key is 'tC', which is the one written late.
candidates.evidence_against: No waveform or per-edge trace is available to prove the exact ordering for transfer 1. The T_slv/T_mst of slv_slow is inferred from the run name and is not shown in the log. The sub-phase at reset (e.g. 'pready', it%6==5) is also not logged.

candidates.evidence_for: The message, taken literally, says the requester got PREADY for a transfer with no completer completion edge. If the RTL could raise o_apb_pready without a slv-side PREADY handshake, the result would look like this.
candidates.evidence_against: In the RTL, reg_pready (mst.sv:215) comes only from w_load_resp/w_ack_event (mst.sv:137,184), which depends on the synchronized ack. The ack toggles only on w_done = ACCESS & i_apb_pready (slv.sv:139,179). The completer model also requires psel/penable/rdy before it builds a cpl entry with 'resp' (test:388-398), and 'resp' is present. All SVA protocol checks report fails=0 (slv_slow.s1.log:525-542). CHK-029 order S0<psel<C<PREADY passes in 2000-transfer runs including this config (test_chk_029 PASS, slv_slow.s1.log:475), and the same test passes in 13 other configurations.

candidates.evidence_for: CHK-028 (contract.json:862-864) says what happens to the interrupted transfer and to traffic after release. It does not say how a transfer that completed just before the reset should be scored, or when 'C' has to be known relative to the reset. The spec (line 149, 533) defines only 'in flight' transfers as lost.
candidates.evidence_against: C is defined clearly as a rising i_clk_slv sampling event (contract.json:947), and PREADY must follow C (contract.json:948). A transfer that has delivered PREADY has completed. It is not in flight, and the spec gives one clear answer for it. The gap is in the testbench's sampling, not in the spec.

analyses.options: Fix test (recommended; does not weaken any check): make the completer's record of C available before score() runs. (a) Record C at the rising edge itself: add a RisingEdge(i_clk_slv) monitor that writes cur['tC']=now() when o_apb_psel=1, o_apb_penable=1 and i_apb_pready=1 are sampled, which matches the contract.json:947 definition. Or (b) store the time rdy=1 was driven (test:396) and, in score(), derive tC as the first e.es entry after it, if no tC exists yet. Or (c) in test_chk_028, after assert_resets/kill (test:959-960), wait for the next FallingEdge(i_clk_slv) plus a small Timer so the completer coroutine (and the hand fix at test:335-339) runs before score(e, partial=True) at test:967. Option (c) still relies on the e.t_rst > t hand fix. (a) or (b) removes the race at its source. With any of these, keep the check at test:560 as it is. Fix RTL: none indicated. The RTL produces PREADY only after a real slv-side completion (slv.sv:139/179, mst.sv:137/184/215), and all SVAs pass. Clarify spec (optional): in CHK-028 expected (contract.json:864), state that a transfer whose requester PREADY was sampled before the reset assertion is a completed transfer and is scored with its completion edge C, and that only transfers without PREADY count as lost.
